audit_findings.title: Parent-share numerator is mixed with consolidated-basis add-backs
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable income is combined with consolidated D&A, impairment, capital-expenditure, working-capital, or bridge amounts before division by parent shares, allowing noncontrolling-interest amounts into common-share owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Net loss attributable to noncontrolling interests was $120 million in 2025 compared to $5 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The basis mismatch is demonstrated, but its net size is not. The filed $120 million FY2025 noncontrolling-interest loss equals 11.0% of the $1,086.7 million anchor, but $107 million arose from the Sensia impairment and therefore cannot be treated as the OE correction. Component-level ownership data are required to establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a subsidiary-level reconciliation of every FY2025 OE and bridge adjustment, apply Rockwell's economic ownership percentage, and rerun all scenarios using the parent-only anchor and bridge.

audit_findings.title: Sensia dissolution invalidates the null perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF projects pre-dissolution FY2025 OE while the June 2026 shares, cash, investments, and debt bridge reflect a post-dissolution company.
audit_findings.evidence: The transaction is expected to close in the first half of fiscal 2026 subject to customary closing conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: Sensia dissolved on April 1, 2026. Rockwell derecognized $94 million of net assets, received a $40 million cash payment, recorded a $20 million pre-tax gain, and identified $62 million of divested-business comparative quarterly sales. Retained operations, divested operations, settlements, transaction costs, and the reported margin benefit have opposing effects, so those filed amounts do not establish the recurring OE correction. A structural change to the forecasted business is reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Build a pro forma FY2025 continuing-OE statement for the businesses retained by Rockwell, remove divested Sensia operations and nonrecurring impairment, gain, and transaction costs, reconcile the $40 million settlement and working-capital payment to June 2026 cash, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Asbestos accrual may have been added back while the cash claim was omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: $151 million net exposure; $1.33 per share; 0.95% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A $91 million noncash accounting-method charge may be added back to OE while the related future cash payments are absent from both projected OE and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We recorded pre-tax expense in Other (expense) income in the Consolidated Statement of Operations of $ 136 million for the year ended September 30, 2025 ($ 103 million after tax or $ 0.91 per share), which includes charges for a change in accounting method of $ 91 million and indemnity accrual increase of $ 45 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission must be corrected if present, but even deducting the entire filed $151 million net asbestos exposure directly from equity would reduce the $15,934 million base value by only 0.95%, or approximately $1.33 per share. Discounting the scheduled payments through 2060 would produce a smaller effect. This cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $433.81 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $91 million cash-flow add-back and all asbestos cash payments in the OE calculation; recognize the obligation exactly once through projected payments or a $151 million bridge deduction.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may receive credit without its announced investment cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Scenario growth is applied mechanically to FY2025 OE without an explicit deduction for incremental capitalized and expensed investment required to generate that growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We plan to invest over $2 billion over the next five years in manufacturing facilities, digital infrastructure, and talent to support market share growth, operational resilience, and margin expansion.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed program exceeds $2 billion over five years, averaging more than $400 million annually, compared with FY2025 capital expenditures of $186 million, FY2026 expected capital expenditures of $270 million, and anchor OE of $1,086.7 million. The record does not separate maintenance spending, incremental growth capital, digital infrastructure, or expensed talent costs, so the valuation effect is unquantified; however, the disclosed scale is reasonably capable of materially reducing distributable OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the five-year spending schedule split between maintenance capex, growth capex, capitalized digital investment, and expensed costs; deduct incremental reinvestment from each scenario's OE and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 Pillar Two tax increase is absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.51 million annual tax on FY2025 pre-tax income; approximately $386.5 million of base equity value or $3.42 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 after-tax OE anchor is projected into FY2026 and later years without the recurring increase in cash taxes, overstating after-tax OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Enactment of this regulation in its current form would generally apply to the Company beginning in fiscal year 2026, resulting in an approximate increase in our effective tax rate of 3 percent as well as in the amount of global corporate income tax paid.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated: the June 2026 filing confirms Pillar Two was applied and says the adjusted effective tax rate rose to 19.2% from 16.7% primarily because of it. Applying the filed three-percentage-point estimate to FY2025 pre-tax income of $917 million gives $27.51 million annually. Scaling that reduction through the base-case operating-PV ratio reduces value by approximately $3.42 per share, or 2.43% of base value, which does not change the conclusion against the $433.81 price.
audit_findings.action: Normalize continuing pre-tax OE after the Sensia perimeter adjustment, apply the recurring Pillar Two tax burden from FY2026, and rerun all scenarios to document the corrected values.

audit_findings.title: Retirement-benefit funding may be an unbridged legacy claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $162 million net funded deficit; $1.43 per share; 1.02% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Legacy pension or postretirement underfunding should reduce the equity bridge or future OE, while current-service costs should remain in recurring OE and must not be counted twice.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to contribute $ 23 million related to our global pension plans and $ 6 million to our postretirement benefit plans in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed September 2025 funded deficits are $121 million for pensions and $41 million for postretirement benefits, totaling $162 million. Even a full direct bridge deduction would reduce the $15,934 million base equity value by only 1.02%, or approximately $1.43 per share. The expected $23 million pension and $6 million postretirement contributions for 2026 do not establish an additional recurring claim because their legacy, current-service, and discretionary portions are not separated.
audit_findings.action: Update the funded-status reconciliation to the valuation date, classify the $29 million expected contributions between legacy underfunding and current service, and recognize any legacy amount exactly once in the bridge or projected OE.
